```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Park 2023 relates the steady-state trough serum concentration of bevacizumab
to overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) in non-squamous
non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), using the patients of the phase III study
that compared the biosimilar SB8 with EU-sourced reference bevacizumab. The two
endpoints were fitted as two separate parametric time-to-event models with the
same structure, so they are packaged as two model files and validated together
here:

* `modellib("Park_2023_bevacizumab_os")` -- overall survival.
* `modellib("Park_2023_bevacizumab_pfs")` -- progression-free survival.

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Park_2023_bevacizumab_os")()$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2023.1288308>

Both models use a log-logistic baseline hazard with scale `lambda` (months) and
shape `gamma`,

$$h_0(t) = \frac{\gamma}{\lambda} \frac{(t/\lambda)^{\gamma - 1}}{1 + (t/\lambda)^{\gamma}},$$

which the trough concentration reduces by a constant fraction through an
inhibitory sigmoid Emax term (Park 2023 Equation 4):

$$h(t) = h_0(t) \left(1 - \frac{E_{max} \, C_{trough}^{Hill}}{EC_{50}^{Hill} + C_{trough}^{Hill}}\right).$$

The survival function therefore has the closed form
$S(t) = (1 + (t/\lambda)^{\gamma})^{-(1 - EFF)}$, and the median time to event is
$\lambda (2^{1/(1 - EFF)} - 1)^{1/\gamma}$. That median is exposed by both
models as the derived output `medtte`, as in the supplementary NONMEM control
file. With no drug effect the median is `lambda` itself.

The Hill coefficient is fixed at 20, which makes the exposure effect close to a
switch: below about 70 ug/mL the drug has almost no effect on the hazard, and
above about 90 ug/mL the effect is at its maximum. The treatment (SB8 versus
reference) was tested as a covariate and had no effect on either endpoint, so
the models have no treatment term and apply to both products.

There is no PK layer. `CTROUGH` is a data column holding one observed trough
per patient (the pre-dose sample before cycle 7, or before cycle 5 for three
patients), applied unchanged over the whole follow-up.

# Population

The analysis used the 224 patients of study SB8-G31-NSCLC (NCT02754882) who had
a steady-state trough concentration: 100 on SB8 and 124 on reference
bevacizumab, each given 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks with paclitaxel and
carboplatin for 4-6 induction cycles and then as maintenance monotherapy (Park
2023 Methods). Per Park 2023 Table 1, 41.5% were female, 69.2% were younger than
65 years, 92.9% were white, 93.3% had adenocarcinoma and 99.6% stage IV
disease, and 67% had ECOG performance status 1. Median (Q1-Q3) body weight was
72.1 (64.2-82.0) kg and median trough concentration 119.5 (92.0-150.5) ug/mL
(115.1 for SB8 and 125.5 for the reference product).

The same information is available programmatically via each model's
`population` metadata (`readModelDb("Park_2023_bevacizumab_os")()$population`).

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry carries an in-file comment naming its source location. The
equations come from the Supplementary Material NONMEM control file (overall
survival; Park 2023 Equations 3 and 4 give the same structure for both
endpoints).

| Equation / parameter | OS value | PFS value | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `llambda` (log-logistic scale, months) | 12.0 | 8.28 | Table 3, row lambda |
| `lgamma` (log-logistic shape) | 3.67 | 3.94 | Table 3, row gamma |
| `lemax` (maximum fractional hazard reduction) | 0.704 | 0.451 | Table 3, row EMAX |
| `lec50` (ug/mL) | 77.5 | 77.7 | Table 3, row EC50 |
| `lhill` | 20 (fixed) | 20 (fixed) | Table 3, row HILL (no RSE); Results, "tested with a range of 1-100, and a value of 20 was fixed" |
| `etallambda` | 0 (fixed) | 0 (fixed) | Supplementary control file `LAMDA = THETA(1)*EXP(ETA(1))`; no variance reported |
| Log-logistic hazard `H1/H2` with `DEL = 1e-6` | -- | -- | Supplementary control file `$DES`; Equation 3 |
| Hazard scaled by `(1 - EFF)`, sigmoid Emax `EFF` | -- | -- | Supplementary control file `$PK` / `$DES`; Equation 4 |
| `medtte` closed form | -- | -- | Supplementary control file `MEDTTE` |
| Time unit = months | -- | -- | Figure 3 and Figure 6 axis labels |

# Typical-value checks against the paper

Park 2023 reports, for each endpoint, the drug-free and maximum median time to
event (Figure 6), the medians at 50% and 90% of the way between them, and the
trough concentrations that reach those medians (`TTE50CONC`, `TTE90CONC`). The
supplementary control file finds the concentrations by stepping the trough from
0 to 150 ug/mL in 0.1 ug/mL steps and keeping the largest one whose median is
still at or below the target. The chunk below reproduces that search with the
packaged models, one simulated subject per concentration.

```{r typical-grid}
mod_os <- readModelDb("Park_2023_bevacizumab_os")
mod_pfs <- readModelDb("Park_2023_bevacizumab_pfs")

conc_grid <- seq(0, 150, by = 0.1)
grid_events <- data.frame(
  id = seq_along(conc_grid),
  time = 0,
  evid = 0,
  cmt = "cumhaz",
  CTROUGH = conc_grid
)

median_by_conc <- function(mod, endpoint) {
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
    events = grid_events,
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  stopifnot(nrow(sim) == length(conc_grid))
  data.frame(endpoint = endpoint, CTROUGH = sim$CTROUGH, medtte = sim$medtte)
}

grid <- bind_rows(
  median_by_conc(mod_os, "OS"),
  median_by_conc(mod_pfs, "PFS")
)

tte_summary <- grid |>
  group_by(endpoint) |>
  summarise(
    base = medtte[CTROUGH == 0],
    max_med = max(medtte),
    med50 = base + 0.5 * (max_med - base),
    med90 = base + 0.9 * (max_med - base),
    tte50conc = max(CTROUGH[medtte <= med50]),
    tte90conc = max(CTROUGH[medtte <= med90]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
stopifnot(nrow(tte_summary) == 2)

published <- data.frame(
  endpoint = c("OS", "PFS"),
  base = c(12.0, 8.28),
  max_med = c(22.2, 10.5),
  med50 = c(17.1, 9.38),
  med90 = c(21.2, 10.3),
  tte50conc = c(82.4, 79.7),
  tte90conc = c(92.2, 89.1)
)

comparison <- tte_summary |>
  pivot_longer(-endpoint, names_to = "quantity", values_to = "simulated") |>
  inner_join(
    pivot_longer(published, -endpoint, names_to = "quantity", values_to = "published"),
    by = c("endpoint", "quantity")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated - published) / published)
stopifnot(nrow(comparison) == 12)

comparison |>
  mutate(
    quantity = recode(
      quantity,
      base = "Drug-free median (months)",
      max_med = "Maximum median (months)",
      med50 = "50% of maximum median (months)",
      med90 = "90% of maximum median (months)",
      tte50conc = "TTE50CONC (ug/mL)",
      tte90conc = "TTE90CONC (ug/mL)"
    )
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Endpoint" = endpoint,
    "Quantity" = quantity,
    "Simulated" = simulated,
    "Park 2023" = published,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r typical-assert}
# Deterministic quantities computed from the published point estimates, so a
# tight bound is appropriate. The drug-free median is lambda exactly; the
# maximum medians are read from Figure 6 (about 22.2 and 10.5 months), and the
# others are printed in the Results. The 0.1 ug/mL search step and the
# three-significant-figure estimates in Table 3 leave a residual of at most
# 0.6% (TTE50CONC 82.5 versus 82.4 ug/mL for OS, 79.8 versus 79.7 for PFS).
stopifnot(all(abs(comparison$pct_diff) < 1.5))
```

## Closed-form survival identity

The ODE integrates the hazard numerically; the survival it returns must equal
the closed form for every trough concentration.

```{r closed-form}
check_conc <- c(0, 60, 77.5, 82.4, 92.2, 150)
cf_events <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  CTROUGH = check_conc,
  time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)
) |>
  mutate(id = match(CTROUGH, check_conc), evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz") |>
  arrange(id, time)

closed_form_error <- function(mod) {
  theta <- mod$theta
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = cf_events, returnType = "data.frame")
  stopifnot(nrow(sim) == nrow(cf_events))
  lambda <- exp(theta[["llambda"]])
  gamma <- exp(theta[["lgamma"]])
  emax <- exp(theta[["lemax"]])
  ec50 <- exp(theta[["lec50"]])
  hill <- exp(theta[["lhill"]])
  eff <- emax * sim$CTROUGH^hill / (ec50^hill + sim$CTROUGH^hill)
  s_cf <- (1 + (sim$time / lambda)^gamma)^-(1 - eff)
  max(abs(sim$sur - s_cf))
}

cf_err <- c(
  OS = closed_form_error(rxode2::rxode2(mod_os)),
  PFS = closed_form_error(rxode2::rxode2(mod_pfs))
)
cf_err
# Numerical integration against its own closed form: the only difference is
# solver error (default rtol 1e-6), so the bound is tight.
stopifnot(all(cf_err < 1e-4))
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-6, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 6 of Park 2023: median OS and PFS versus steady-state
# trough concentration, with the observed median troughs of SB8 (115.1 ug/mL)
# and reference bevacizumab (125.5 ug/mL).
fig6_events <- data.frame(
  id = 1:541,
  time = 0,
  evid = 0,
  cmt = "cumhaz",
  CTROUGH = 0:540
)
fig6 <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_os), events = fig6_events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(endpoint = "Median overall survival (months)"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pfs), events = fig6_events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(endpoint = "Median progression-free survival (months)")
)

ggplot(fig6, aes(CTROUGH, medtte)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 115.1, colour = "blue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 125.5, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(
    x = "Steady-state trough concentration (ug/mL)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Park 2023. Blue: SB8 median trough; red: reference median trough."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Virtual cohort and population survival curves

The visual predictive checks of Park 2023 (Figures 3-5) simulate the observed
cohort with its own trough concentrations. The individual troughs are not
published, so the cohort here takes the 224 troughs as evenly spaced quantiles
of a log-normal distribution matched to the pooled median and interquartile
range of Table 1 (119.5, 92.0-150.5 ug/mL). Using quantiles rather than random
draws makes the cohort, and every check on it, deterministic. With the
between-subject variance fixed at zero, the population survival curve is the
mean of the individual survival curves.

```{r cohort}
n_cohort <- 224
trough_sdlog <- (log(150.5) - log(92.0)) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_cohort),
  CTROUGH = qlnorm(ppoints(n_cohort), meanlog = log(119.5), sdlog = trough_sdlog)
) |>
  mutate(quartile = paste0("Q", ntile(CTROUGH, 4)))
stopifnot(abs(median(cohort$CTROUGH) - 119.5) < 1)

cohort_events <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25)) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz")

population_survival <- function(mod, endpoint) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = cohort_events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    left_join(select(cohort, id, quartile), by = "id") |>
    mutate(endpoint = endpoint)
}
cohort_sim <- bind_rows(
  population_survival(mod_os, "Overall survival"),
  population_survival(mod_pfs, "Progression-free survival")
)
stopifnot(length(unique(cohort_sim$id)) == n_cohort)
```

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates the model-predicted median curves of Figure 3 of Park 2023.
pop_curve <- cohort_sim |>
  group_by(endpoint, time) |>
  summarise(sur = mean(sur), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(pop_curve, aes(time, sur)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (months)",
    y = "Survival probability",
    caption = "Replicates the predicted median curves of Figure 3 of Park 2023."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Figure 3 of Park 2023 shows the predicted median overall-survival curve
crossing 0.5 at about 19.5-20 months and reaching about 0.40 at 24 months, and
the progression-free curve crossing 0.5 at about 10 months and reaching about
0.08 at 24 months.

```{r figure-3-assert}
pop_median <- pop_curve |>
  group_by(endpoint) |>
  summarise(
    median_months = approx(sur, time, xout = 0.5, ties = mean)$y,
    sur_24 = sur[time == 24],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
pop_median
stopifnot(nrow(pop_median) == 2)
os_row <- pop_median[pop_median$endpoint == "Overall survival", ]
pfs_row <- pop_median[pop_median$endpoint == "Progression-free survival", ]
# Figure 3 read-offs. The cohort is an approximation of the observed troughs
# (log-normal quantiles), so the bounds are sized for that, not for solver
# error.
stopifnot(
  abs(os_row$median_months - 19.75) < 1.5,
  abs(os_row$sur_24 - 0.40) < 0.05,
  abs(pfs_row$median_months - 10) < 1,
  abs(pfs_row$sur_24 - 0.08) < 0.04
)
```

```{r figure-4-5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates the model-predicted median curves of Figures 4 (OS) and 5 (PFS)
# of Park 2023: population survival stratified by trough-concentration
# quartile.
quartile_curve <- cohort_sim |>
  group_by(endpoint, quartile, time) |>
  summarise(sur = mean(sur), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(quartile_curve, aes(time, sur, colour = quartile)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (months)",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "Trough quartile",
    caption = "Replicates the predicted median curves of Figures 4 and 5 of Park 2023."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Only the lowest trough quartile, whose troughs straddle `ec50`, has
noticeably shorter survival; the upper three quartiles sit on the plateau of
the exposure-response curve.

# PKNCA validation

Not applicable. The models contain no pharmacokinetics: the trough
concentration is an input column and the outputs are a hazard, a survival
probability and a median time to event, none of which is a concentration-time
profile. The typical-value checks and the closed-form identity above take the
place of the NCA comparison.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No between-subject variability.** The control file puts an exponential
  random effect on `lambda`, but Table 3 reports no variance and the
  Discussion states that typical predictions were made. `etallambda` is
  carried at `fixed(0)`.
* **Progression-free survival structure.** The supplementary control file is
  the overall-survival one. Park 2023 Equations 3 and 4, the Results text and
  Table 3 give the same log-logistic sigmoid-Emax structure for progression-free
  survival, so `Park_2023_bevacizumab_pfs` uses the same equations with the
  Table 3 PFS estimates.
* **Time unit.** Table 3 does not print units for `lambda`. Figures 3 and 6 are
  in months and the drug-free medians of Figure 6 (12 and about 8.3 months)
  equal `lambda`, so time is in months.
* **The trough is time-fixed.** One trough per patient, measured at steady
  state, applies from randomisation onward, including the induction cycles
  before steady state. A user simulating a new regimen should supply that
  regimen's steady-state trough, not a time-varying concentration.
* **Virtual cohort.** The troughs of the 224 patients are not published. The
  population curves above use log-normal quantiles matched to the Table 1
  median and interquartile range, which is why the Figure 3 comparison has
  read-off-sized rather than solver-sized tolerances.
* **Maximum medians.** Park 2023 prints the 50% and 90% medians and
  concentrations but not the maximum median itself; 22.2 and 10.5 months are
  read from the plateaus of Figure 6.

# Errata

No published erratum was found for Park 2023 (Europe PMC, checked 2026-10-29).
